P·07  ·  CONSTRUCTION  ·  ON THE VF BUILD SLATE

Site Truth EngineThe site says what happened.
Every day. In writing.

Construction runs on claimed progress, and settles its disputes over what happened months later, at legal rates. Site Truth Engine reads the cameras a site already has and produces the daily record: what advanced, what stalled, what looks unsafe, what arrived.

WHY IT HAS TO EXIST

An industry that builds everything
and can’t prove what it did yesterday.

Construction’s productivity, rework and dispute problems share one root: the absence of a trusted, continuous record of what happened on site. The evidence infrastructure already exists: it is bolted to the scaffolding, recording footage that no one on the project reviews.

F·01

Productivity flatlined

McKinsey’s landmark analysis put construction productivity growth at roughly 1% a year over two decades, trailing nearly every other industry. You cannot improve a process you cannot see.

F·02

Rework eats the margin

Industry studies place direct rework at around 5% of project cost, with broader estimates running to 10–25% once knock-on effects count. Much of it traces to work proceeding on top of unverified prior work.

F·03

The site is the danger zone

Eurostat attributes roughly a quarter of all fatal workplace accidents in the EU to construction, the deadliest major sector. Risk conditions are visible in footage long before they are visible in reports.

F·04

Disputes settle on bad memory

Arcadis has reported average construction-dispute values in the tens of millions of dollars, fought largely over what happened when. A continuous visual record changes the economics of the argument.

For everyone whose money
or name is on the build.

The small and mid-size contractor

The enterprise site-intelligence players sell to megaprojects. Site Truth Engine starts with the contractor running three to ten sites on cameras they already bought: the operator who needs the truth layer most and whom the enterprise players priced out first.

EXISTING CCTVMULTIPLE SMALL SITESNO BIM TEAMPRICED FOR SMEs

Site & project managers

The morning site-state briefing generated overnight: progress against plan, flagged conditions for human review, deliveries logged. The walk-around becomes verification.

Developers & owners

Independent progress truth on the asset being paid for: drawdown decisions and contractor conversations grounded in the record.

Safety officers

Risk conditions (blocked routes, missing edge protection, unsafe storage) flagged for qualified human review. The system watches the work and the site; it never rates the workers.

Quantity surveyors & insurers

Valuations, claims and premiums built on continuous visual evidence: the daily record that today exists only as contested recollection.

WHAT IT CHANGES

From dead footage
to a living record.

The wedge is deliberate: no new hardware estate, no BIM prerequisite, no six-month integration. Point the engine at the cameras the site already has, load the plans, and the record starts tonight.

Progress, verified.

Work-in-place detected and matched against the programme: observed percent-complete replaces claimed percent-complete, dated and archived.

Risk seen early.

Hazardous conditions surfaced from the footage and queued for the safety officer’s judgement: a second set of eyes that does not tire, and never a verdict.

The dispute-proof diary.

A timestamped visual site diary that accumulates by itself: the evidence layer for delay claims, valuations and handover, built as a by-product of running.

THE MECHANICS

Cameras in.
Accountability out.

The engine treats the site’s existing CCTV as a sensor array, runs vision models against plans and programme, and publishes everything into one reviewable record, with worker privacy engineered in from the start.

Every VF system runs on the harness stack, is steered by the Helmsman engine and is watched from a command dashboard.

LAYER 1

The intake layer

Connects to existing site cameras (fixed CCTV, time-lapse units, periodic capture), normalising whatever the site already runs. New hardware is an option, never the ticket price.

LAYER 2

The vision core

Detection models for structural elements, plant, materials and site conditions, tuned per project phase. Trained to watch work and environment; faces are irrelevant to it and it treats them accordingly.

LAYER 3

The truth ledger

Observations reconciled against drawings and programme into an append-only site record: progress states, flagged conditions, delivery events, with every entry dated, sourced, and exportable as evidence.

LAYER 4

The review surface

Dashboards and morning briefs for managers; a flag queue for safety review; owner views scoped to their asset. Humans confirm; the engine never acts alone.

One site watched,
then the industry’s memory.

PLANNED
QUESTIONS

Asked.
Answered.

Do I need new cameras?

No. The intake layer connects to the cameras a site already runs (fixed CCTV, time-lapse units, periodic capture) and normalises whatever is there. New hardware is an option, never the ticket price. There is no BIM prerequisite and no six-month integration: point the engine at existing cameras, load the plans, and the record starts.

What does Site Truth Engine record?

Progress verified against the programme, so observed percent-complete replaces claimed percent-complete. Risk conditions such as blocked routes, missing edge protection and unsafe storage, queued for a safety officer. Deliveries and materials flow. Everything lands in an append-only, timestamped site diary with each entry dated, sourced and exportable as evidence.

Does it monitor workers?

It watches the work and the site, and never rates the workers. The vision core is trained on structural elements, plant, materials and conditions; faces are irrelevant to it and it treats them accordingly. Flagged conditions go to qualified human review. Humans confirm; the engine never acts alone.

Who is it built for?

The small and mid-size contractor running three to ten sites on cameras they already bought, the operator the enterprise players priced out first. Site and project managers get a morning brief, developers and owners get independent progress truth, safety officers get a flag queue, and quantity surveyors and insurers get continuous visual evidence.

When does it ship?

Site Truth Engine is in build. The first phase runs live pilots on working sites: camera intake, progress detection against plans, the daily brief and site diary proven with real contractors. Risk-condition flagging with safety-officer review loops and multi-site views follow, then general availability with QS and insurance export formats. Pilot sites get the truth layer first.
